title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
grouping: Three panels in one row with no frames, each closed by a serif sub-caption '(a) ... (PPL 43.2)', '(b) ...', '(c) ...' carrying the panel's perplexity in bold colour; the panels grow in content from left to right (baseline, intermediate fix, proposal).
shapes_depth: Matrices are flat grids with values printed in every cell: the FP16 weight matrix in pale orange cells with signed decimals, the quantized matrix Q(W) in pale blue cells with signed integers, joined by an arrow labelled Q. The activation X is a wide grid tinted as a red heat map with one saturated column. In (b) one row of Q(W) stays orange with an orange 'FP16 channel' tag; in (c) the blue rows of Q(W) take different blue intensities after scaling. Thin curved and dotted arrows carry handwritten-style serif labels ('determine the salient weights by activation', 'average mag.', 'scale before quantize', alpha).
proposed_highlight: The bit width is written as a coloured subscript on each matrix name (Q(W) with a green 'INT3', 'MixPrec' for the mixed one); the drawback of (b) is a red callout ('bad hardware efficiency') with a curly arrow; perplexities are coloured red for the bad baseline and green for the two good ones; the proposal is the last panel.
lesson: Write the bit width as a coloured subscript on the matrix name (Q(W) INT3, MixPrec) and leave the high-precision channel as a differently tinted row inside the low-bit matrix, so precision is read from colour rather than from text.
notes: Figure 2, but it plays the teaser role (three approaches compared, proposal last). Venue from the PDF footer ('Proceedings of the 7th MLSys Conference ... 2024').

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: architecture other: no network is drawn; the figure compares transformations of one weight matrix (round-to-nearest, mixed precision, per-channel scaling)

core.what: three side-by-side captioned panels built on the same weight-matrix grid - (a) round-to-nearest, (b) keep 1% salient weights in FP16, (c) scale before quantization - with the proposal last and each caption ending in its perplexity

relations.form: panels (a), (b), (c) left to right, each ending in a 4-column weight grid labelled Q(W) with its precision subscript, and a bold coloured PPL value in each caption (red 43.2, green 13.0, green 13.0)

the operation is drawn on small matrices with printed values: FP16 cream grid -> INT3 blue grid in (a); in (b) one cream FP16 row left inside the blue INT3 grid; in (c) the weight rows shaded by their scale

in (b) and (c) a pink activation matrix X lies beside the weight grid with a '*' between them, its one dark-red salient column matching the weight row it selects (dotted 'determine the salient weights by activation' arrow in (b))
in (c) X -> 'average mag.' arrow up to a one-row pink scale vector alpha -> curved 'scale before quantize' arrow into the weight grid, whose row 2 turns saturated blue

channels.colour: cream = FP16 values, blue = INT3 values (blue saturation in (c) = scaling applied per row), pink-to-red shade = activation magnitude; red/green in captions and subscripts = bad/good result - red thus means both 'large activation' and 'bad', and green both 'INT3' subscript and 'good PPL'
channels.shape: grids of numbered cells = matrices; a single-row grid = the per-channel scale vector
channels.line: solid arrows = operations (Q, average, scale); dotted curved arrow = selection by activation; a red curly arrow points the 'bad hardware efficiency' note at the MixPrec label
channels.frame: no frames; panels are separated by whitespace and their sub-captions

quality.strengths: the comparison is geometry - three panels on the same matrix vocabulary, ours last, each scored in its caption; the method is drawn on its structure (a salient activation column selects the matching weight row, kept FP16 in (b), scaled in (c)), so the reader sees why scaling replaces mixed precision; data drawn as real numbers in the grids
quality.weaknesses: red and green each carry two meanings (activation magnitude / bad result; INT3 subscript / good result); the (c) weight grid drops its printed values, so the effect of scaling on the quantised numbers is shown only by shade; the X-to-W correspondence relies on counting columns against rows, with no tie line

insights.structure: Three side-by-side captioned panels (a) RTN quantization, (b) keep 1% salient weights in FP16, (c) scale before quantization, each built around a small weight matrix and, in (b) and (c), an activation matrix X multiplied into it.
insights.data: Weights are grids with printed numbers (cream FP16 values, blue INT3 integers), activations are pink grids whose shade marks magnitude with one salient red column, and the per-channel scale is a single pink row labelled alpha.
insights.emphasis: Captions carry perplexity in bold with colour (red 43.2 vs green 13.0), and in (b) one cream FP16 row inside the blue INT3 grid plus a red 'bad hardware efficiency' note marks the trade-off that (c) removes.
insights.flow: Read left to right as a progression of solutions; inside panels a dotted curved arrow goes from the salient activation column to the weight row and an 'average mag.' arrow leads up to the alpha row.
insights.avoid: The tiny numbers in every cell are unreadable at print size and add no information beyond the colour coding.

arrangement.units: three uncontained captioned panels of numeric/colour-shaded matrix grids
arrangement.inputs_as: FP16 weight matrix grid; activation matrix X below in (b),(c)
arrangement.shared: the same activation pattern X appears in (b) and (c)
